messages:
Seong: Heads-up — seeing a spike of 504/502 from IPv6-only mobile clients hitting the edge in us-west-2. Only when clients resolve AAAA for api.redwood.example.com. IPv4 clients unaffected.
Maya: Can you paste a `curl -6 -v` and say which LB type this is (ALB/NLB)?
Seong: Quick paste: `curl -6 -v https://api.redwood.example.com` -> TLS handshake completes, then HTTP/1.1 502 from the load-balancer.
Seong: `dig AAAA api.redwood.example.com @1.1.1.1` returns two AAAA records. tcpdump on gateway pod shows no IPv6 SYN incoming. `kubectl get svc redwood-api -o yaml` shows no explicit IPv6 target IPs; annotations include `external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/hostname: api.redwood.example.com` and `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ip-address-type: dualstack` (but not sure LB actually provisioned v6).
Alex: FYI ALB dualstack behavior is subtle — ALB will lease an IPv6 address but backend connectivity often still goes IPv4. If the target group is IP mode you need to give IPv6 addresses to targets; otherwise ALB does translation on the node ENI level. NLB has separate semantics.
Olivia: We've seen carriers that use DNS64/NAT64; if our AAAA points to an IPv6 address that doesn't really forward to the backend, DNS64 will synthesize and route to IPv4 but TLS SNI and proxy layers can break. Could be a mismatch in SNI or ALPN causing 502. :thinking_face:
Jon: Quick check from my laptop: `dig AAAA api.redwood.example.com @8.8.8.8` -> no AAAA. `dig AAAA api.redwood.example.com @our-resolver` -> AAAA exists. So edge DNS setup (external-dns/Cloudflare) is publishing AAAA while LB hasn't fully wired.
Clara: deploy-bot: rolling canary for api-gateway finished 20m ago — any chance a recent change toggled annotations?
deploy-bot: [deploy] Canary deploy api-gateway v23.4 -> rolled back automatically due to spike in 5xx from IPv6 probes.
Maya: Temporary mitigation: remove the AAAA records for the affected apis in the zone (external-dns/Cloudflare) so IPv6-only clients fall back through carrier DNS64/NAT64. It's not ideal but fast. Note: adding IPv4 egress NATs per AZ to support IPv6-translated traffic adds ~ $700-1200/mo/region in our estimates.
Alex: Long-term: either 1) make the LB truly dualstack -> ensure service endpoints (targets) have IPv6 addresses (CNI + ENI/ipam changes), or 2) front the LB with a small fleet of dualstack proxies that accept IPv6 and proxy to IPv4 backends, or 3) move to ALB/NLB configuration that guarantees IPv6 <-> IPv4 handling. Each option has infra and cost tradeoffs.
Seong: Plan: disable AAAA for us-west-2 api host, run dualstack validation in staging (include `curl -6`, `tcpdump -i any ip6`, and end-to-end TLS checks), and schedule a runbook item to evaluate proxy fleet vs native dualstack by next sprint. I'll open an incident ticket.
Olivia: Please add a PD alert for AAAA->5xx regressions and include a sample `curl -6` check in the alert runbook.
Maya: For the record, sample k8s annotation we used to test dualstack in staging:
```
metadata:
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ip-address-type: "dualstack"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  loadBalancerSourceRanges: ["0.0.0.0/0","::/0"]
```
Maya: Also run `dig +short AAAA api.redwood.example.com @<resolver>` and `curl -6 -v` as smoke tests after any DNS change.
Seong: Thanks — I'll post the incident ticket link here once created. :thumbsup:
